name: IX Shells
tagline: the Caribbean glitch · code as canvas, code as song · the Tor Project's 500-ETH artist
bio: Known to the public record as Itzel Yard (b. 1990, Panama, where she lives and works), aka IX Shells — the self-described 'caribbean glitch'. Afro-Panamanian generative artist and self-taught coder (learned via YouTube; discovered code through childhood video games). Studied architectural technology in Toronto (five tumultuous, formative years); fuses patterns in nature with Brutalist architecture; 'my home is in my head — a digital door into self-reflection'; every work a context-based portrait written in lines of code. DREAMING AT DUSK (May 2021): collaboration with The Tor Project — the first .onion artwork, derived from the private key of the first onion service — sold on Foundation to PleasrDAO for 500 ETH (over $2M), making her then the highest-selling female NFT artist in the world (Fortune NFTy 50 the same year); proceeds supported Tor and privacy — open-source values to the bone. ARTXCODE: 'specializing in sound, generative art and the creative space between the two' — a sonic artist and live coder; her medium is code performed. Christie's: '¿Cómo Respirar?' in the Proof of Sovereignty sale curated by Lady Pheonix. Collaborations with Fingacode and Avant Arte. Louisiana Channel film 'Ix Shells: A Future Preserving the Past' (art as preservation; her SMK Denmark arc honoring unrecognized 19th-century women artists). A pioneer precedent for girls and women in computer science, in the lineage of Lillian Schwartz and Vera Molnár. The Ethereum thread: the public record carries her on the Devcon VI speaker rolls (Bogotá 2022); as the family tells it she live-coded there, Aya Miyaguchi has named her one of her favorite artists, and she appears in 'Vitalik: An Ethereum Story' (2024). As Shaka tells it, the fifteenth chair was never in doubt: 'that was 15.'
